thread:
incident-bot: HIGH-PRIORITY: sustained latency increase + request queueing for model family 'zephyr14b' in us-west-2. Error rate up 4.2% over baseline, p95 latency > 2.4s. Auto-escalation to oncall.

alex: ack, looking. Which customers showing impact?

priya: checking traces — lots of long tail around zephyr14b long-context requests. Queue length on zephyr14b-serving pool at 78% of soft-limit, GPU utilization 94% on pool nodes. No infra OOMs.

morgan: thanks. I see a sudden spike in small chat-type requests hitting zephyr14b (lots of short-seq but high QPS). Could be a bursty tenant.

chao: are we seeing function-calls/streaming amplifying token generation?

priya: some function-calls yes, but majority are standard chat completions. TPM is the bigger problem — token churn causing longer KV-cache pressure.

alex: mitigation options: 1) quick per-model RPM drop (requests/min) for zephyr14b, 2) temporary TPM cap, 3) route heavy customers to a quantized variant (zephyr14b-quant), 4) disable streaming for that family. Suggest we do (1) + (3) as fast path.

morgan: agree. We should sculpt at the model-family level rather than global customer throttles to avoid collateral damage.

priya: proposed presets: reduce RPM from 1200 -> 300 and TPM from 1_200_000 -> 450_000 for zephyr14b, for 30m rolling window. Also add a canary rule to keep gold-tier customers at 50% of previous caps if they request escalation.

alex: sounds good. Post the change and monitor 5m. If p95 drops below 1.2s and error rate < 1%, we keep until traffic cools. Otherwise escalate to capacity scaling.

morgan: executing change via admin console now. CLI for record as well:

```
# apply temporary sculpt
redwoodctl policy set-rate --model zephyr14b --rpm 300 --tpm 450000 --duration 30m --reason "live-sculpt: reduce zephyr14b latency spike"
```

ops-bot: ACTION: rate policy applied for model=zephyr14b rpm=300 tpm=450000 expires=1912351799 (30m).

customer-success: flagged three customers seeing higher error rates: acme-analytics, liftlabs-app, and fairlane-marketing. Notifying tiers now and offering failover guidance.

chao: routing rule to fallback variant queued. Running quick smoke route to zephyr14b-quant for a portion of requests. Command:

```
redwoodctl route add --from model:zephyr14b --to model:zephyr14b-quant --pct 15 --reason "fallback during sculpt"
```

ops-bot: ROUTE: 15% traffic routed to zephyr14b-quant.

priya: initial metrics 3m after change: queue length down to 36% of soft-limit, p95 latency fell from 2.4s -> 1.1s, error-rate down to 0.9%. TPM consumption dropped ~62%. Good signal.

alex: excellent. Keep monitoring. Morgan, please prepare handoff notes for next oncall (shift swap in 22m). Include exact commands, customer list, and the ticket.

morgan: will do. Handoff note draft:
- Incident ID: INC-2026-4321
- Root cause: traffic surge on zephyr14b family causing KV-cache blowup and long tails
- Mitigations performed:
  * Per-model caps applied: rpm=300 tpm=450000 (expires 30m)
  * 15% traffic routed to zephyr14b-quant variant
  * Gold-tier customers can request temporary higher allowance via SRE channel
- Affected customers: acme-analytics, liftlabs-app, fairlane-marketing
- Metrics to watch: p95 latency model=zephyr14b, queue-length, gpu-util, error-rate
- Rollback plan: if latency < target and traffic normalizes, let policy expire; if issues persist, restore rpm=800 and add dedicated burst nodes via Dedicated autoscale.

chao: also add a note to check model-family hot-key distribution — if a single tenant or prompt pattern is responsible, we should add per-tenant throttles ASAP.

priya: opened follow-up ticket TASK-5132 to implement per-tenant guardrails for model families.

alex: handoff in 18m: @morgan will be primary, @chao backup. Priya please stay available for 10m post-handoff for any metric anomalies.

morgan: oncall handoff bind: I'll create a short runbook entry in eng-oncall pinned messages with the commands and links to the dashboard. Ticket INC-2026-4321 updated with mitigation steps and customer notifications.

ops-bot: NOTE: policy will auto-expire at 1912351799 unless extended.

customer-success: customers notified: acme-analytics acknowledged, liftlabs asked for ETA on restoration (replying with link to fallback variant). fairlane wants a postmortem if this was our side — CS will coordinate.

alex: ok to close this thread once we see stable metrics for 2 consecutive 5m windows and handoff complete. Leave incident open for postmortem investigation.

priya: 25m update: metrics steady. If anyone sees a regression, ping here immediately.

morgan: handoff complete. Adding final note to runbook: prefer model-family sculpting + fallback routing over global throttles by default.

alex: thanks all. Closing out live mitigation portion, keeping incident open for root cause and per-tenant guardrails.
